welcome.title: Welcome to your AI company
welcome.what: You set your name, language and workspace.

vision.title: What do you want to build?
vision.what: Describe your idea or existing business in your own words, add details and documents if you have them.
vision.ai: Reads your answers and documents (saved in Company Brain) to plan its research.
vision.next: The AI researches your market, competitors and customers.

intelligence.title: The AI researches your business
intelligence.what: AI research tasks analyse the idea, market, competitors, customers, business model, opportunities and risks.
intelligence.ai: Runs real research tasks (with live web search when a research provider is connected) and saves each deliverable in Company Brain.
intelligence.next: The findings become your Company Blueprint.

blueprint.title: Your Company Blueprint
blueprint.what: Departments, products, goals, objectives, projects and workflows — proposed from the research, edited by you.
blueprint.ai: Drafts the blueprint; nothing is created until you approve it.
blueprint.next: Your approved company gets its AI team.

workforce.title: Hire your AI workforce
workforce.what: Your AI team as an org chart: a CEO, managers and specialists with responsibilities and goals.
workforce.ai: Proposes the team for your blueprint; you decide who is hired.
workforce.next: You launch into the Command Center.

launch.title: Your company is ready
launch.what: Everything that now exists, and what the AI keeps building after launch.
launch.ai: Keeps working in the background: positioning, go-to-market, launch and financial plans.
launch.next: Run your company from the Command Center.

maintenanceMode.normal: The platform is open. Customers can sign in and work normally.
maintenanceMode.changed: The platform is closed for customers. They see the maintenance page; administrators keep working.
maintenanceMode.flip: Every customer page shows the maintenance page and all customer APIs answer 503 until you turn it off.
maintenanceMode.restore: Customers can use the platform again right away.

readOnlyMode.normal: Customers can read and change their data.
readOnlyMode.changed: Customers can look at their data but no change is saved.
readOnlyMode.flip: Every change made through the platform is refused for every company. Reading still works.

aiWorkforceEnabled.normal: AI employees are allowed to work for every company.
aiWorkforceEnabled.changed: The AI workforce is off. No AI task can be created or run anywhere.
aiWorkforceEnabled.flip: Turning this off stops all AI work for every company. Running tasks stop and no new task can start.
aiWorkforceEnabled.restore: AI employees can work again. Companies need to start new tasks themselves.

aiExecutionPaused.normal: The worker picks up AI tasks as soon as they are created.
aiExecutionPaused.changed: AI tasks are paused. New tasks wait in the queue and nothing is lost.
aiExecutionPaused.flip: AI tasks keep queuing but none is run until you resume. Good for a short pause.
aiExecutionPaused.restore: Waiting AI tasks start running again in order.

registrationsEnabled.normal: New people can create an account.
registrationsEnabled.changed: Sign-up is closed. New visitors see “registrations closed”.
registrationsEnabled.flip: Nobody new can sign up until you turn it back on. Existing users are not affected.
registrationsEnabled.restore: New people can sign up again.

companyCreationEnabled.changed: No organization can create a new company.
companyCreationEnabled.flip: Every organization is blocked from creating new companies. Existing companies keep working.

automationsEnabled.normal: Workflows run on their schedules and triggers.
automationsEnabled.changed: Automations are off. Schedules, triggers and runs are skipped.
automationsEnabled.flip: All workflow automations stop for every company. Skipped runs are not made up later.
automationsEnabled.restore: Workflows run again from their next schedule or trigger.

backgroundJobsPaused.normal: Background jobs and event handlers run normally.
backgroundJobsPaused.changed: All background jobs are paused. Events keep queuing.
backgroundJobsPaused.flip: Every background job stops (emails, syncs, module jobs). Events wait and run when you resume.
backgroundJobsPaused.restore: Background jobs resume and work through the waiting events.

leads.what: Leads are people or companies who might buy from you.
leads.why: Every sale starts as a lead — keeping them here means nobody is forgotten.
leads.can: Add leads, see who is hot, plan follow-ups and let AI research them.

contacts.what: Contacts are the people you talk to at your customers.
contacts.why: Knowing who decides and who uses your product helps you win and keep deals.
contacts.can: Add people, link them to companies and see every conversation.

accounts.what: Accounts are the companies you sell to or work with.
accounts.why: One place per company shows its people, deals and history.
accounts.can: Add companies, merge duplicates and ask AI for an account analysis.

deals.what: A deal is a sale you are working on, with a value and a stage.
deals.why: Deals tell you how much money is on the way and what needs attention.
deals.can: Create deals, move them through stages, mark them won or lost.

pipeline.what: The pipeline shows all open deals as cards in their stage.
pipeline.why: You see at a glance where deals get stuck.
pipeline.can: Drag deals between stages and spot stale ones.

proposals.what: Proposals are written offers you send to a customer.
proposals.why: A clear offer with prices is often what closes a deal.
proposals.can: Create offers from deals, send them and track if they were viewed or accepted.
proposals.next: Pick a deal to write an offer

calendar.what: The calendar shows follow-ups, meetings and expected closing dates.
calendar.why: Showing up on time is half of selling.

dashboard.what: Numbers about your leads: how many, where they are, who owns them.
dashboard.why: It shows if your sales engine is healthy.
dashboard.can: Check conversion between stages and overdue follow-ups.

import.what: Bring customers in from a spreadsheet, or take them out.
import.why: Start with the data you already have instead of typing it again.
import.can: Import CSV files and export your CRM.

settings.what: How your sales process is set up: stages, sources, fields and rules.
settings.why: A process that fits how you sell keeps everyone on the same page.
settings.can: Edit stages, automate assignments and describe your ideal customer.

customers.what: Customers are companies that already buy from you.
customers.why: Keeping customers happy is the cheapest way to grow.
customers.can: See every customer, their people, deals and history.

today.what: Your to-do list for selling: the one best next step for every open lead and deal.
today.why: Sales are won by following up at the right moment — this list makes sure nothing slips.
today.can: Do each step with one click. Emails are only drafted; you approve before anything is sent.

discover.what: Describe who you sell to and we search the web for matching businesses.
discover.why: New customers start with a list of the right people to talk to.
discover.can: See real search results with their source, and turn the good ones into leads.

outreach.what: Personal emails to leads and customers — written by you or drafted by AI.
outreach.why: A short, personal email is the fastest way to start a conversation.
outreach.can: Draft, edit, approve and send through your own connected email. Nothing is sent without approval.

sequences.what: A sequence is a series of follow-up emails and reminders sent on a schedule.
sequences.why: Most deals need several follow-ups; a sequence does the remembering for you.
sequences.can: Write the steps once, add people, and it stops by itself when someone replies.

meetings.what: Every sales meeting you booked with a lead, contact or deal.
meetings.why: Meetings are where deals move forward — prepare and record what was agreed.
meetings.can: Download calendar files, mark meetings done with notes, or cancel them.

prospecting.what: An AI sales assistant that finds the right people at companies that match your ideal customer, checks their work email and writes the first email.
prospecting.why: New customers start with conversations. The autopilot fills your pipeline every day while you decide how much it may do on its own.
prospecting.can: Set up who to reach in plain words, watch the real funnel, approve emails and keep a do-not-contact list.

rules.title: How it stays safe
rules.verified: Only verified email addresses are contacted unless you opt in to unverified ones, which get a lower daily limit and always wait for your approval.
rules.unsubscribe: Every email carries a one-click unsubscribe link; unsubscribing stops all sales and marketing email.
rules.stop: It stops for a person as soon as they reply, an email bounces or they unsubscribe.
rules.caps: Daily limits for new people and emails are never exceeded, including follow-ups.
rules.consent: The lawful basis for contacting is stored on every lead it creates.

health.how1: Every KPI you may see is compared with the previous 30 days. Flat is 50; better is higher, worse is lower (direction-aware: fewer overdue tasks is better).
health.how2: Each department's score is the average of its KPIs; the company score weights finance and sales more than other departments.
health.how3: Open problems (drops, overdue work, expiring approvals, failed AI work) lower the score: 6 points for critical, 2 for warnings.
health.how4: No AI is involved — the same data always gives the same score.
health.insightsHint: "Do this" hands the problem to AI Command: it plans the work, delegates it to your AI employees and asks before changing anything.
health.forecastHint: A straight trend line through the last 12 weeks, extended 4 weeks ahead. Dashed parts are projections.
health.noForecast: Projections need at least 6 weeks of history for a flow KPI such as revenue.
health.lowFit: The history is irregular, so this projection is unreliable.
health.projectionNote: Projected change of the next {weeks} weeks vs the last {weeks}.

insight.forecast_decline: {metric} is projected to change {change}% over the next 4 weeks
insight.department_weak: {department} scores {score} of 100 — most of its KPIs got worse

do.metric_drop: Why did {metric} change {change}% this week, and what should we do about it?
do.metric_attention: {metric} is {value}. Find the cause and propose how to fix it.
do.overdue_work_tasks: We have {count} overdue work tasks. Re-plan them and propose new dates and owners.
do.overdue_follow_ups: We have {count} overdue CRM follow-ups. Draft the follow-ups and prioritise them.
do.approvals_expiring: Summarize the {count} approval requests that expire within 24 hours and recommend a decision for each.
do.ai_tasks_failed: {count} AI tasks failed recently. Find out why and propose how to fix it.
do.ai_employee_over_budget: {name} has used this month's AI budget. Recommend how to rebalance the work.
do.forecast_decline: {metric} is projected to change {change}% in the next 4 weeks. Explain why and propose a plan to change the trend.
do.department_weak: {department} is under-performing (score {score}). Diagnose the causes and propose an improvement plan.

integrations.subtitle: Connect the tools your company runs on. Credentials are encrypted and every action is audited.
integrations.noneConnected: No integrations are connected yet. Pick one from the marketplace to get started.

google.description: Gmail, Google Calendar and Drive for email, meetings and files.
google.sync: Meetings sync both ways with Google Calendar (7 days back, 60 days ahead).
google.setup: Enable the Gmail, Google Calendar and Drive APIs for the platform's Google OAuth app.

microsoft.description: Outlook mail, calendar and Teams messages.
microsoft.sync: Meetings sync both ways with the Outlook calendar (7 days back, 60 days ahead) when Google Calendar is not connected.
microsoft.setup: Register an app in Microsoft Entra ID with the listed Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.

slack.description: Post messages to Slack channels from workflows and alerts.
slack.setup: Create a Slack app at api.slack.com/apps with the listed bot scopes.

stripe.description: Import payments and react to new revenue with workflows.
stripe.sync: Successful charges after the connection date become “Payment received” events.
stripe.setup: Create a restricted key in the Stripe Dashboard → Developers → API keys (read balance and charges; write prices and payment links if you send payment links).

whatsapp.description: WhatsApp Business Cloud API for customer messaging.
whatsapp.setup: In Meta Business Suite create a system user token with whatsapp_business_messaging and copy the phone number ID from WhatsApp Manager.
whatsapp.settingsHelp: Optional: your Meta app secret, so Realy can verify the signature of WhatsApp webhooks.

hubspot.description: Import HubSpot contacts and companies into your CRM.
hubspot.sync: Contacts are imported and deduplicated by email; their companies become accounts, matched by domain.
hubspot.setup: Create a public app in your HubSpot developer account with the listed scopes.

salesforce.description: Import Salesforce contacts and accounts into your CRM.
salesforce.sync: Contacts changed since the last sync are imported and deduplicated by email; accounts are matched by domain or name.
salesforce.setup: Create a Connected App in Salesforce Setup with OAuth enabled and the listed scopes.

linkedin.description: Publish posts to LinkedIn on behalf of a member.
linkedin.setup: Create an app at developer.linkedin.com with “Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect” and “Share on LinkedIn”.

x.setup: Create a project and app at developer.x.com with OAuth 2.0 (confidential client) and read/write permissions.

facebook.description: Publish to and read engagement from Facebook Pages.
facebook.setup: Create a Meta app (Business type) with Facebook Login and request the listed Page permissions.

instagram.description: Publish content to an Instagram business account.
instagram.setup: Link each Instagram professional account to a Facebook Page; the Meta app needs the listed Instagram permissions.

quickbooks.sync: Customers become CRM accounts and contacts; invoices are imported once as Finance drafts in your base currency.
quickbooks.setup: Create an app at developer.intuit.com with the Accounting scope.

xero.sync: Customer contacts become CRM accounts and contacts; sales invoices are imported once as Finance drafts in your base currency.
xero.setup: Create a web app at developer.xero.com/app/manage.

webhook.description: Receive signed HTTP callbacks from any system and trigger workflows.
webhook.setup: Create an incoming webhook below and paste its URL into the sending system.

custom_api.description: Call any HTTPS API with an API key from your workflows.
custom_api.setup: Get an API key for the service and note its base URL and authentication header.

google_ads.settingsHelp: Optional: use your own developer token (otherwise the platform's) and the manager account ID to log in through.
google_ads.description: Google Ads customer accounts: campaigns, spend and conversions.
google_ads.setup:
Enable the Google Ads API in Google Cloud and get a developer token from a Google Ads manager account (API Center).
The platform admin sets GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN, or you enter your own token in the connection settings.

openai.description: Quick rewrites, summaries and image generation with your own OpenAI account.
openai.setup:
Create a secret key at platform.openai.com → API keys (a project key is recommended).
Optionally set a default model and your organization ID.

gemini.description: Google Gemini models for text features, as a fallback to OpenAI.
gemini.setup: Create an API key in Google AI Studio (aistudio.google.com → Get API key).

tavily.description: Real-time web search for AI employees and research features (primary provider).
tavily.setup: Sign in at app.tavily.com and copy your API key (starts with tvly-).

exa.description: Neural web search with page contents; first fallback for web research.
exa.setup: Create an API key in the Exa dashboard (dashboard.exa.ai → API keys).

serpapi.description: Google search results through SerpApi; second fallback for web research.
serpapi.setup: Copy your private API key from serpapi.com → Your account → API key.

stability.description: Stable Image models for marketing visuals.
stability.setup: Create an API key at platform.stability.ai → Account → API keys and make sure the account has credits.

replicate.description: Run open image and video models (Flux, MiniMax and more) on Replicate.
replicate.setup:
Create an API token at replicate.com → Account → API tokens and add billing.
Optionally choose the image and video models to run.

runway.description: AI video generation from text or an image with Runway.
runway.setup: Create an API key in the Runway developer portal (dev.runwayml.com) and buy API credits.

youtube.description: Upload and manage videos on your YouTube channels.
youtube.setup: In Google Cloud, enable the YouTube Data API v3 for the platform's OAuth app.

tiktok.description: Publish videos to your TikTok account.
tiktok.setup: Create an app at developers.tiktok.com with Login Kit and Content Posting API, and request the listed scopes.

threads.description: Publish posts to Threads and read their insights.
threads.setup: Create a Meta app with the Threads API use case at developers.facebook.com and add the threads permissions.

pinterest.description: Create pins on your Pinterest boards.
pinterest.setup: Create an app at developers.pinterest.com and request standard access for the listed scopes.

meta_ads.description: Facebook and Instagram ad accounts: campaigns, spend and results.
meta_ads.setup: Add the Marketing API product to the platform's Meta app and request ads_management (advanced access).

linkedin_ads.description: LinkedIn Campaign Manager ad accounts and reporting.
linkedin_ads.setup: Request the Advertising API product for the platform's LinkedIn app (developer.linkedin.com).

tiktok_ads.description: TikTok for Business advertiser accounts and reporting.
tiktok_ads.setup: Create a developer app at business-api.tiktok.com and set its advertiser redirect URL to the redirect URI below.

google_search_console.description: Search clicks, impressions and queries of your verified sites.
google_search_console.setup: Enable the Google Search Console API in Google Cloud for the platform's OAuth app; sign in with an account that owns the sites.

wordpress.description: Publish articles to a self-hosted or WordPress.com site.
wordpress.setup:
In WordPress go to Users → Profile → Application Passwords, add one named “Realy” and copy it.
The site must use HTTPS and allow the REST API.

webflow.description: Publish CMS items to your Webflow sites.
webflow.setup: In Webflow open Site settings → Apps & integrations → API access and generate a site token with CMS read/write.

shopify.description: Your Shopify store: products, blog articles and orders.
shopify.setup: In Shopify admin go to Settings → Apps → Develop apps, create an app with the Admin API scopes you need, install it and copy the Admin API access token.

sendgrid.description: Send your company's emails from your own SendGrid account and domain.
sendgrid.setup:
Create an API key with Mail Send permission at app.sendgrid.com → Settings → API Keys.
Verify the sender address or domain under Sender Authentication.

mailchimp.setup: Create an API key under Profile → Extras → API keys; the server prefix is the part after the dash (e.g. us21).

twilio.description: SMS and WhatsApp messages from your Twilio numbers.
twilio.setup:
Copy the Account SID and Auth token from the Twilio Console home page.
Add a sender number (or messaging service SID) for SMS and an approved WhatsApp sender if you use WhatsApp.

razorpay.description: Payment links and payments with Razorpay (India).
razorpay.setup: Generate API keys in the Razorpay Dashboard → Account & Settings → API keys (test or live mode).

s3.description: Store generated images, videos and files in your own S3-compatible bucket (AWS, R2, B2, MinIO...).
s3.setup:
Create a bucket and an access key limited to it (s3:PutObject, s3:GetObject, s3:ListBucket).
For Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2 or MinIO enter the endpoint; leave it empty for AWS.

cloudflare.description: Cloudflare account access (DNS, R2, Pages) for infrastructure automation.
cloudflare.setup:
Create an API token at dash.cloudflare.com → My Profile → API Tokens with only the permissions you need.
Optionally enter the account ID to use.

vapi.description: AI voice agents that place and answer phone calls (Realy phone team).
vapi.setup:
Copy your Private API key from the Vapi dashboard (Organization → API Keys).
Realy creates the assistants, numbers and webhooks for you.

retell.description: AI voice agents with built-in call analysis (Realy phone team).
retell.setup:
Create an API key in the Retell dashboard (Settings → API Keys). Use a key with the webhook badge: Realy verifies call events with it.
Realy creates the agents and webhooks for you.

apollo.description: B2B contact data: decision makers by role and seniority, verified work emails and company details for the prospecting autopilot.
apollo.setup: In Apollo go to Settings → Integrations → API, create a master API key and paste it here.

hunter.description: Find and verify work email addresses; also finds people at a company domain.
hunter.setup: Copy your API key from hunter.io → API (dashboard → API keys).

pdl.description: People Data Labs: optional extra source for people and company enrichment.
pdl.setup: Copy your API key from the People Data Labs dashboard → API keys.

openrouter.description: One key for hundreds of AI models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Mistral…) with real per-request cost.
openrouter.setup:
Create a key at openrouter.ai → Keys (set a credit limit if you like).
Optionally choose a default model such as openai/gpt-4.1-mini.

openai_compatible.description: Any API that speaks the OpenAI chat format — Together, Groq, Fireworks, Mistral, DeepSeek or your own gateway.
openai_compatible.setup:
Enter the provider's base URL ending in /v1 (it must be public HTTPS).
Paste an API key and the exact model name; Realy checks the model is listed.

elevenlabs.description: Natural voices for voiceovers and calls, a voice library and Scribe transcription.
elevenlabs.setup:
Create an API key in ElevenLabs → Developers → API keys (enable Text to Speech, Voices and Speech to Text).
Optionally paste a default voice ID from the Voice Library.
elevenlabs.settingsHelp: Optional: the signing secret of an ElevenLabs webhook pointing to the callback URL above.

deepgram.description: Fast, accurate speech to text for calls, meetings and videos (Nova models).
deepgram.setup:
Create an API key in the Deepgram console → API Keys (Member role is enough).
Optionally set the model, e.g. nova-3.

luma.description: Luma Dream Machine: cinematic text- and image-to-video generation (Ray models).
luma.setup:
Create an API key at lumalabs.ai → API (billing must be set up).
Optionally choose a default model such as ray-2.

kling.description: Kling AI official API: text- and image-to-video with strong motion and realism.
kling.setup:
In the Kling developer console create an Access Key / Secret Key pair (resource package required).
Realy signs a short-lived token with them for every request; the base URL defaults to the global endpoint.

shotstack.description: Render videos from templates and timelines (captions, music, overlays) at scale.
shotstack.setup:
Copy the API key from the Shotstack dashboard → API Keys.
Choose the environment: stage (free, watermarked) or v1 (production).

creatomate.description: Template-based video and image rendering for ads, social posts and personalised clips.
creatomate.setup:
Copy the project API key from Creatomate → Project settings → API key.
Design templates in Creatomate; Realy fills their elements when rendering.

twilio_voice.description: Phone calls on your own Twilio numbers: outbound calls, status callbacks and call recordings.
twilio_voice.setup:
Copy the Account SID and Auth token from the Twilio Console home page.
Optionally set the default caller number; your voice numbers are listed after connecting.

sip_trunk.description: Bring your own carrier: SIP trunk details for voice platforms that dial over SIP.
sip_trunk.setup:
Ask your carrier for the SIP domain, username and password of the trunk.
Choose the transport (UDP, TCP or TLS) and the caller ID the carrier allows.

pipedrive.description: Import people from Pipedrive into your CRM and create deals there.
pipedrive.setup: In Pipedrive open your avatar → Personal preferences → API and copy your personal API token.
pipedrive.sync: Imports Pipedrive people as contacts (deduplicated by email) with their organisations.

notion.description: Search your Notion workspace and create pages and database rows from Realy.
notion.setup:
Create an internal integration at notion.so/profile/integrations and copy its secret.
Share the pages or databases Realy may use with the integration (••• → Connections).

clickup.description: Create ClickUp tasks from Realy in the workspace and list you choose.
clickup.setup: In ClickUp open Settings → Apps and generate your personal API token (pk_…).

calendly.description: Event types and one-time booking links; new bookings and cancellations become CRM meetings.
calendly.setup:
In Calendly open Integrations & apps → API and webhooks and generate a personal access token.
Realy registers the booking webhook for you (webhooks need a paid Calendly plan; otherwise meetings are imported by the scheduled sync).
calendly.sync: Imports upcoming bookings (and cancellations) as CRM meetings — a safety net for missed webhooks.

google_drive.description: Save and read files in Google Drive (only files Realy creates or you open with it).
google_drive.setup:
Sign in with Google and approve file access.
Realy only gets access to files it creates or that you open with it, plus file names for search.

zendesk.description: Read and create Zendesk tickets so agents and AI can follow up on customer issues.
zendesk.setup:
In Zendesk Admin Center → Apps and integrations → Zendesk API, enable token access and add an API token.
Enter your subdomain (yourcompany for yourcompany.zendesk.com) and the agent email the token belongs to.
zendesk.settingsHelp: Optional: the signing secret of a Zendesk webhook pointing to the callback URL above.

intercom.description: Read Intercom conversations and reply or add notes from Realy.
intercom.setup: In the Intercom Developer Hub create an app for your workspace and copy its access token (Authentication).
intercom.settingsHelp: Optional: your Intercom app's client secret, used to verify webhook signatures.

plaid.description: Read-only bank feeds: balances and transactions from 12,000+ banks, staged for reconciliation.
plaid.setup:
Copy the client ID and the secret for your environment from dashboard.plaid.com → Developers → Keys.
Choose sandbox to try it (user_good / pass_good) or production for real banks, then link your banks on this page.
plaid.sync: Pulls new, changed and removed transactions of every linked bank and refreshes balances.

wise.description: Read-only balances of your Wise Business account in every currency.
wise.setup:
In Wise open Settings → Integrations and tools → API tokens and create a read-only token.
Choose production (or sandbox for a Wise sandbox account).
wise.sync: Refreshes the balances of each Wise profile.

revolut_business.description: Read-only balances and transactions of your Revolut Business account.
revolut_business.awaiting: Revolut Business offers no simple API keys: its API requires a certificate-signed OAuth client per company. Realy will add it once that flow is supported — until then use Plaid (where Revolut is available) or import a CSV statement in Finance.

zapier.description: Start any Zap from Realy events and workflows with a signed webhook.
zapier.setup:
In Zapier create a Zap with the trigger "Webhooks by Zapier → Catch Hook" and copy its URL.
Realy sends one labelled test event when you connect. To let a Zap call Realy, create an incoming webhook under Integrations → Webhooks.

make.description: Run Make scenarios from Realy events and workflows with a signed webhook.
make.setup:
In Make add a "Webhooks → Custom webhook" module to a scenario and copy its address.
Realy sends one labelled test event when you connect so Make can learn the data structure.

n8n.description: Trigger n8n workflows (cloud or self-hosted) from Realy with a signed webhook.
n8n.setup:
Add a Webhook node (POST) to your workflow, activate it and copy the production URL (it must be public HTTPS).
Optionally set a signing secret and verify the x-realy-signature header in the workflow.

jamendo.description: Royalty-free music under Creative Commons licenses that allow commercial use, for video soundtracks.
jamendo.setup: Create an app at devportal.jamendo.com and paste its Client ID.

integrations.notConfiguredBody: Create an OAuth app with the provider and set these environment variables on the web app and the worker, then restart:

webhooks.incomingHelp: Endpoints other systems can POST to. Every accepted delivery becomes a “Webhook received” event that can trigger workflows.
webhooks.outgoingHelp: Send your company's events to your own endpoints, signed, with automatic retries.
webhooks.name: Name
webhooks.secretOnce: Copy this secret now — it will not be shown again.
webhooks.rotateConfirm: Rotate the secret? The current secret stops working immediately.
webhooks.deleteConfirm: Delete this webhook and its delivery log?
webhooks.workflowHint: Use this endpoint as a workflow trigger (Workflows → trigger “Incoming webhook”). Top-level JSON fields are available as event.data.FIELD.
webhooks.deliveriesHelp: The last 100 requests, including rejected ones.
webhooks.urlHint: Must be a public HTTPS URL.
webhooks.signatureHelp: Each request carries the headers X-Realy-Event, X-Realy-Delivery and X-Realy-Signature in the form t=TIMESTAMP,v1=SIGNATURE, where SIGNATURE is the hex HMAC-SHA256 of TIMESTAMP + "." + body using your signing secret. Recompute it to verify, and reject old timestamps.
webhooks.retryHelp: Failed deliveries are retried after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h and 6 h, then marked failed. Redeliver any delivery manually.
webhooks.signingSecretHint: Copy it from the provider's webhook settings. Requests are verified with it via the {header} header; it is stored encrypted and never shown again.
webhooks.presetSaved: Endpoint created. Paste its URL into the provider's webhook settings — requests signed with your secret are accepted, everything else is rejected and logged.
webhooks.presetHelp: Paste this URL into the provider's webhook settings. Each request must carry a valid {provider} in the {header} header; unsigned, tampered or replayed requests are rejected and logged below.

logs.help: API calls made through this connection and its sync runs.

guide.what: Your company's connections to outside tools — email, payments, CRM, ads and more. AI, research, voice and media providers are included and run on the platform account.
guide.why: Every connection is verified with the provider and health-checked daily, so features never pretend to send, sync or charge when they cannot.
guide.ai: AI employees use connected tools only through approved actions; anything external waits for your approval and every call is logged with its cost.
guide.nextFix: {count, plural, one {# integration needs} other {# integrations need}} attention — open it to test or reconnect.
guide.nextMore: Connect the next tool your team uses every day — check what each one unlocks below.
guide.nextFirst: Start with the tool you use most: connect it and Realy verifies the credentials immediately.

not_configured.title: Background worker not configured
not_configured.body: Scheduled syncs, webhook retries and daily connection health checks run on the worker service, which needs Redis (REDIS_URL). Manual actions on this page still work.

stale.title: Background worker is not responding
stale.body: The worker stopped sending heartbeats. Scheduled syncs, webhook deliveries and health checks are paused until it is running again.

missing.title: Background worker has not started
missing.body: No worker heartbeat has been recorded yet. Start the worker service (see docs/deployment.md) to run scheduled syncs, webhook deliveries and health checks.

providerWebhook.title: Provider callbacks
providerWebhook.autoRegistered: Realy registered this webhook at the provider for you — nothing to set up.

security.token: Only this connection's secret URL is accepted; keep it private.
security.signed: Every callback must also carry the provider's valid signature; unsigned or altered requests are rejected.

how.token: Realy passes this URL to the provider as the completion callback of each job it starts. You can also paste it in the provider's dashboard.
how.TWILIO: Realy sets this as the status and recording callback on calls it places. For inbound calls or SMS status, paste it in the number's settings in the Twilio Console.
how.CALENDLY: New bookings and cancellations become CRM meetings, linked to the contact with the invitee's email.
how.META: In your Meta app → WhatsApp → Configuration, set this callback URL and verify token, and save the app secret in the settings below so Realy can verify signatures.
how.ELEVENLABS: Add this URL as a webhook in ElevenLabs (Settings → Webhooks) and save its signing secret in the settings below.
how.PLAID: Realy registers this URL on every bank you link, so new transactions are pulled as soon as Plaid has them. Plaid's signed JWT is verified on each call.
how.ZENDESK: Create a webhook in Zendesk Admin Center → Apps and integrations → Webhooks with this URL, then save its signing secret in the settings below.
how.INTERCOM: In the Intercom Developer Hub → your app → Webhooks, set this URL and save the app's client secret in the settings below.

providerEvents.title: Received events
providerEvents.help: Callbacks this provider sent, after signature verification. Only summaries are stored.

bank.title: Bank feed

help.plaid: Read-only: Realy reads balances and transactions of the banks you link and stages them for reconciliation. It can never move money.
help.wise: Read-only balances of your Wise profiles, refreshed with each sync. Statements need Wise's strong customer authentication and are not pulled.

bank.linked: {count, plural, one {# bank linked. Transactions arrive with the next sync.} other {# banks linked. Transactions arrive with the next sync.}}
bank.nothingLinked: No bank was linked in that Plaid session.
bank.removeConfirm: Unlink {name}? Its access is revoked at Plaid and its staged transactions are deleted from Realy.
bank.noBanks: No bank linked yet. Link one to stage its transactions for reconciliation.
bank.noTransactions: No transactions staged yet. They appear after the first sync.
bank.reconcileHint: Staged transactions are matched against your books in Finance.

platform.title: Availability
platform.availableBody: {name} runs on the platform account. There is nothing to connect or configure: features that use it work right away.
platform.unavailableBody: {name} is not available yet. The platform administrator has not enabled it, so features that need it stay off until then.
platform.disabledBody: {name} is turned off on the platform right now.
platform.usageBody: Your usage counts against your plan limits and appears in your usage and cost reports. You never need your own API key.
platform.providerDisabled: {name} is turned off on the platform right now, so it cannot be connected. An existing connection is not used until it is turned back on.
platform.oauthHelp: Connect your own {name} account by signing in. You never enter keys or passwords here.
platform.oauthNotReady: Connecting {name} is not available yet. The platform has not enabled sign-in for it.

new_lead_follow_up.name: New lead → auto-assign + follow-up
new_lead_follow_up.description: Assigns an owner with your CRM rules or a round robin of sales managers, creates a follow-up task due tomorrow and notifies the team.

invoice_overdue_reminder.description: Gives the account owner a payment reminder task, posts to #finance on Slack (when connected) and notifies finance.

ticket_created_notify.name: Ticket created → notify support
ticket_created_notify.description: Urgent and high-priority tickets go to support managers, everything else to the support team.

employee_onboarding.name: Employee joined → onboarding + IT setup

weekly_pipeline_review.name: Weekly pipeline review
weekly_pipeline_review.description: Every Monday at 09:00, creates a task to review open leads and follow-ups.

form_submitted_lead.name: Form submitted → new lead
form_submitted_lead.description: Turns form submissions with an email into CRM leads and notifies sales.

objective_decompose.name: Objective created → AI plan
objective_decompose.description: The AI CEO decomposes a new company objective into milestones, projects and tasks, and the owner is asked to review the plan.

ticket_urgent_on_call.name: Urgent ticket → on-call assignment
ticket_urgent_on_call.description: Assigns urgent tickets to the next support manager in rotation (unless already assigned) and notifies them and the team.

candidate_hired_onboarding.name: Candidate hired → onboarding project
candidate_hired_onboarding.description: Creates an onboarding project with contract, equipment and first-week tasks, starts the HR checklist and notifies HR.

deal_approval_gate.name: Large deal → approval gate
deal_approval_gate.description: Deals above 50,000 need approval from a sales manager within 48 hours before the owner is told to proceed.

lead_research_score.name: Research, score and route new leads
lead_research_score.description: AI researches each new lead, rates it Hot, Warm or Cold, the CRM rules assign an owner, and hot leads alert their owner right away.

start.why: A few minutes a week keeps your books right.
start.can: Add income or expenses, create invoices, track payments and bills.

transactions.what: Every payment in and out of your bank, cash and card accounts.

invoices.what: Invoices are bills you send to customers so they pay you.
invoices.why: No invoice, no money — they also show what you're owed.

estimates.what: Estimates (quotes) are prices you offer before the work.
estimates.why: Agreeing on price first avoids disputes.
estimates.can: Create quotes and turn accepted ones into invoices.

creditNotes.what: Credit notes reduce what a customer owes, e.g. for a refund.
creditNotes.why: They keep invoices and balances correct.
creditNotes.can: Issue credit notes and apply them to invoices.

receivables.what: Receivables are money customers owe you.
receivables.why: Unpaid invoices are cash you've earned but don't have yet.
receivables.can: See who owes what and how late, and send reminders.

bills.what: Bills are invoices you receive from suppliers.
bills.why: Paying on time protects your reputation; not too early protects your cash.
bills.can: Record bills, get them approved and pay them.

payables.what: Payables are money you owe to suppliers.
payables.why: They show what will leave your bank soon.
payables.can: See what's due and plan payments.

approvals.what: Spending that needs someone's OK before it's paid.
approvals.can: Approve or reject bills and claims.

claims.what: Expense claims are costs employees paid themselves.
claims.why: Paying people back quickly keeps them happy.

recurring.what: Payments that repeat: rent, subscriptions, retainers.
recurring.why: Automating them saves time and makes forecasts accurate.
recurring.can: Set up repeating invoices and expenses.

budgets.what: Budgets are spending limits per department.
budgets.why: They stop costs from quietly growing.
budgets.can: Set budgets and compare with actual spending.

vendors.what: Vendors are the suppliers you buy from.
vendors.why: Knowing where money goes helps you negotiate.

cashflow.what: Cash flow is money moving in and out over time.
cashflow.why: A profitable business can still run out of cash.
cashflow.can: See the forecast and plan scenarios.

accounting.what: The full books: chart of accounts, journal, periods, tax.
accounting.why: This is what your accountant needs.

reports.what: Standard reports: profit & loss, balance sheet, cash flow.
reports.why: They answer 'are we making money?' and 'what do we own?'

settings.what: Invoice numbering, due days, taxes and categories.
settings.why: Correct settings make every document right.

alerts.what: Warnings about money that needs your attention right now.
alerts.why: Late payments, a shrinking runway or a blown budget are easier to fix early.
alerts.can: See every alert, why it matters and jump straight to the fix.

learn.what: Every finance word used in Realy, in plain language.

manager.what: Your AI finance manager's desk: the monthly memo, the revenue outlook, budget explanations and tidy books.
manager.why: You see what changed, why, and what to do next, without reading every transaction.

roi.what: Return on spend: AI employees, departments and marketing campaigns.

monthlyPack.what: The month in one page: P&L, cash, burn, budgets, AI spend and ROI.

glossary.tip: Tip: every report and chart in Finance links here when it uses one of these words.

revenue.short: All the money you earn from selling your products or services, before any costs are taken off.
revenue.example: You sell 10 websites at 1,000 each: your revenue is 10,000.

invoice.short: A document you send a customer asking to be paid for what you delivered.
invoice.example: After finishing a project you send an invoice for 2,500, due in 30 days.

receivable.short: Money customers owe you for invoices they have not paid yet.
receivable.example: Three unpaid invoices of 1,000 each mean 3,000 in receivables.

estimate.short: A price offer you send before the work starts; it becomes an invoice once accepted.
estimate.example: You quote 4,000 for a new logo; the client accepts and you turn it into an invoice.

creditNote.short: A document that reduces what a customer owes, for example after a refund or a mistake.
creditNote.example: You invoiced 1,200 but agreed a 200 discount: a credit note of 200 fixes it.

paymentLink.short: A web link where a customer can pay an invoice online by card.
paymentLink.example: You add a payment link to the invoice email and the customer pays in two clicks.

mrr.short: Income you can count on every month from subscriptions or retainers.
mrr.example: 20 clients paying 50 a month give an MRR of 1,000.

arr.short: Your recurring income over a full year: MRR × 12.
arr.example: An MRR of 1,000 means an ARR of 12,000.

expense.short: Money you spend to run the business: rent, software, salaries, travel.
expense.example: A 30 monthly software subscription is an expense.

bill.short: An invoice you receive from a supplier that you have to pay.
bill.example: Your accountant sends a bill for 400, due on the 15th.

payable.short: Money you owe suppliers for bills you have not paid yet.
payable.example: Two open bills of 400 and 600 mean 1,000 in payables.

overdue.short: An invoice or bill whose due date has passed and is still not fully paid.
overdue.example: An invoice due on 1 March and still unpaid on 10 March is 9 days overdue.

costCenter.short: A part of the company (often a department) that you track spending for.
costCenter.example: Marketing is a cost center: all ad and agency costs are tagged to it.

projectCost.short: Everything you spent on one project, compared with what it earned.
projectCost.example: A client project earned 10,000 and cost 6,500, so it made 3,500.

profit.short: What is left after taking all expenses away from your revenue. Negative profit is a loss.

margin.short: Profit as a percentage of revenue: how many cents you keep from each unit you earn.
margin.example: 3,000 profit on 10,000 revenue is a 30% margin.

pnl.short: A report that lists income and expenses for a period and shows whether you made a profit.
pnl.example: Your P&L for March shows 12,000 income, 9,000 expenses and 3,000 profit.

balanceSheet.short: A snapshot on one day of what the company owns (assets), owes (liabilities) and the owners' share (equity).
balanceSheet.example: On 31 December you own 20,000 in cash, owe 5,000, so equity is 15,000.

asset.short: Something the company owns that has value: cash, money owed to you, equipment.
asset.example: Your bank balance and a laptop you bought are assets.

liability.short: Something the company owes: unpaid bills, loans, taxes due.
liability.example: A bank loan of 10,000 is a liability.

equity.short: The owners' share of the company: assets minus liabilities.

cashFlow.short: Money actually coming in and going out of your bank account over time.
cashFlow.example: In May 8,000 came in and 9,500 went out: cash flow was −1,500.

cashBalance.short: How much money you have in your bank and cash accounts right now.
cashBalance.example: Two bank accounts with 4,000 and 6,000 give a cash balance of 10,000.

burnRate.short: How much more cash goes out than comes in each month, on average.
burnRate.example: If 12,000 goes out and 8,000 comes in each month, your burn rate is 4,000.

runway.short: How many months your cash lasts at the current burn rate.
runway.example: 40,000 in the bank with a 4,000 monthly burn gives 10 months of runway.

budget.short: A spending limit you set for a category or department for a period.

variance.short: The difference between what you planned (budget) and what really happened (actual).
variance.example: Budget 2,000, actual 2,300: a variance of 300 over budget.

forecast.short: An estimate of future money, built from open invoices, bills, recurring items and recent trends. It is a projection, not a fact.
forecast.example: Open invoices due next month suggest 6,000 coming in.

ledger.short: The full list of every money movement, grouped by account. Reports are built from it.
ledger.example: The 'Software' ledger account lists every software expense this year.

journalEntry.short: One recorded money movement with matching debit and credit lines that always balance.
journalEntry.example: Paying rent: rent expense goes up 1,000, bank goes down 1,000.

reconciliation.short: Checking that the money in your books matches your real bank statement, line by line.
reconciliation.example: Your bank says 5,240 and your books say 5,240: the account is reconciled.

tax.short: Tax added to prices that you collect from customers and pay to the government.
tax.example: A 100 sale with 20% VAT: the customer pays 120 and you owe 20 in VAT.

accrual.short: Recording income or costs when they are earned or used, not when the cash moves.
accrual.example: Work done in March counts as March revenue even if the client pays in April.

home.metaTitle: Realy — One founder. One platform. An entire company.
home.metaDescription: The AI business operating system: sales, marketing, finance, people, product and support in one place, run with an AI workforce that asks before it acts.
home.lede: Realy brings every department of your company into one system and gives it an AI workforce. You set the direction; AI employees plan, draft and prepare the work — and nothing that changes your business happens without your approval.
home.heroNote: AI employees act through permission-checked tools. Reading is automatic; every change waits for you.

story.title: From an idea to a running company, one approval at a time.
story.lede: Realy is not a chatbot bolted onto your tools. It is the place where your company's work actually lives — so the AI can see the whole picture and you can see everything the AI does.

s1.title: Tell it where you're going
s1.body: Describe a goal in plain words in the Command Center. Realy turns it into objectives, milestones and a plan you can edit.

s2.title: Your AI team plans the work
s2.body: AI employees with clear roles — from an AI CEO to an SDR — break the plan into tasks and delegate to each other along your org chart.

s3.title: They do the work through tools
s3.body: Each role can only use the tools it was given. They read your records and documents, draft emails, proposals and plans, and propose changes.

s4.title: You approve — the company learns
s4.body: Changes and anything external land in Approvals first. Every decision is audited, and the facts you keep in company memory shape every next task.

departments.title: Your whole company, in one connected system.
departments.lede: Each department has its own workspace and its own AI roles, and all of them share one company graph — customers, products, people and documents.

workforce.title: Hire AI employees with real roles, not one generic assistant.
workforce.lede: Realy ships with {count} AI roles across leadership, sales, marketing, finance, people, product, engineering, support and operations. Each has its own instructions, tools and limits, and reports to a manager — ultimately to you.

ladder.title: How much the AI may do on its own

read.title: Reading: automatic
read.body: Searching your documents, reading records and analysing data happens on its own, inside your company only.

change.title: Changing data: needs approval
change.body: Creating leads, projects, invoices or anything else is filed as a proposal. Nothing changes until a person approves it.

external.title: Acting outside: approval and high risk
external.body: Sending an email, publishing or paying is marked high risk and always waits for an explicit human decision.

trust.title: Built so you can hand work to AI without losing control.
trust.lede: The safeguards are part of the platform, not a setting you have to remember.

t1.title: Roles and permissions
t1.body: Every person and every AI tool is checked against granular permissions, scoped to the organization or a single company.

t2.title: Complete audit trail
t2.body: Who changed what, when and why — including every AI proposal and every approval — is recorded in the audit log.

t3.title: Two-factor sign-in and SSO
t3.body: Protect accounts with two-factor authentication and single sign-on for your team.

t4.title: Pause any AI employee
t4.body: Pause a role, cancel a task or reject a proposal at any time. Usage limits keep AI spending predictable.

t5.title: Several companies, one account
t5.body: Run multiple companies inside one organization, each with its own data, team and AI workforce.

t6.title: Five languages, right to left
t6.body: The whole product works in English, German, Arabic, Hindi and Chinese, with proper right-to-left layout for Arabic.

pricing.title: Simple plans, priced for your market.
pricing.lede: Prices are set per country and shown in your local currency. Pick the billing country to see exactly what you would pay.

final.title: Build the company you have in mind — with a team that never sleeps.
final.lede: Join the waitlist and we'll let you know as soon as Realy opens in your market, or create your company today where sign-up is already open.

showcase.lede: A quick look at the surfaces you'll use every day. These are illustrations of the real screens — inside the product, they fill with your own company's data.

workforce.label: AI workforce

approvals.title: Why every AI action in Realy waits for your approval
approvals.excerpt: Autonomy is earned. We designed Realy so that AI can do almost all of the work and none of the deciding.
approvals.intro: The fastest way to lose trust in an AI system is to let it do something you didn't expect. So we started from the opposite end: what if the AI could prepare everything, but change nothing on its own?
approvals.h1: Reading is free, changing is a proposal
approvals.p1: Every tool an AI employee can use is labelled. Tools that only read — searching documents, looking at the pipeline, summarising numbers — run on their own. Tools that change data create a proposal in Approvals instead, with a one-line summary of exactly what would happen.
approvals.h2: External actions are always high risk
approvals.p2: Sending an email, publishing a post or moving money leaves your company. Those tools are marked high risk, and an AI employee can never report one as done unless the provider actually accepted it.
approvals.p3: Each decision is audited and stays attached to its task, so you can always see what was proposed, who decided and why. Facts you keep in company memory are part of every future task — so the team gets more useful over time without ever acting behind your back.

graph.title: One company graph instead of twelve tools
graph.excerpt: AI is only as good as the context it can see. That's why Realy keeps your whole company in one connected model.
graph.intro: Most companies run on a dozen tools that don't know about each other. A deal in the CRM has no idea about the invoice in accounting or the ticket in support. Humans bridge the gaps — AI can't.
graph.p1: In Realy, customers, products, teams, people and documents live in one company graph. Sales, finance, support and product all read from and write to the same records.
graph.p2: When an AI account executive prepares a proposal, it can see the customer's history, the products you sell and the documents that describe them — without anyone copying data between systems.
graph.p3: You can still connect the providers you rely on. Credentials are stored encrypted, and when a provider isn't connected Realy says so plainly instead of pretending something was sent.

languages.title: Built for five languages from day one
languages.excerpt: Great companies are started everywhere. Realy speaks English, German, Arabic, Hindi and Chinese — including right-to-left.
languages.intro: Translation is usually something software adds later. We decided early that Realy would be multilingual at its core, because the founders we build for don't all work in English.
languages.p1: Dates, numbers and currencies follow each locale's conventions. Plurals and grammar are handled properly, so a sentence reads naturally in every language.
languages.p2: For Arabic, the whole interface mirrors: navigation, icons that imply direction, and layouts. We use logical spacing throughout so nothing is an afterthought.
languages.p3: Plans are priced per country and shown in local currency, so what you see on the pricing page reflects the market you're actually in.

docs.title: Guides for running your company on Realy.
docs.lede: Short, practical guides — from creating your company to setting how much your AI workforce may do on its own.
docs.helpBody: Search the help center for quick answers.

createCompany.title: Create your company
createCompany.summary: Sign up, set up your organization and first company, and get to the Command Center.
createCompany.s1p: Create an account with your email and choose your country. Verify your email address from the message we send you. Where it is configured, you can also sign in with an external provider.
createCompany.s2h: Set up your organization and company
createCompany.s2p: An organization holds one or more companies. Onboarding walks you through naming your company and describing what it does, which gives your AI team its first context.
createCompany.s3p: The Command Center shows your goals, what the AI is working on and what waits for you. Describe a goal in the command box to get a first plan.

inviteTeam.title: Invite your team
inviteTeam.summary: Add people to your organization and give them the right roles.
inviteTeam.s1p: From the organization settings, invite people by email. They receive a link to join, and the invitation expires if it isn't used.
inviteTeam.s2p: Roles bundle permissions. Grant them for the whole organization or for a single company, so people only see and change what they should.
inviteTeam.s3p: Team members with the right permissions can assign tasks to AI employees and approve proposals. Every action is recorded in the audit log.

aiEmployees.title: AI employees
aiEmployees.summary: What AI employees are, how to hire them and how their work is tracked.
aiEmployees.s1p: An AI employee is a role — such as AI CFO or SDR — with its own instructions, a fixed list of tools and limits on how much it may do in one task. It cannot use tools outside that list.
aiEmployees.s2p: Hire roles in the AI Workforce and place them in your org chart. Managers can delegate to their reports, and anyone can escalate a blocker to their manager.
aiEmployees.s3p: Every piece of AI work is a task you can open: its instructions, sources, tool calls and result. Usage is tracked per day and limits keep spending predictable.

approvals.title: Approvals and autonomy
approvals.summary: How Realy decides what AI may do on its own and what needs a person.
approvals.s1p: Tools that only read run automatically. Tools that change data are supervised: they create an approval request instead of acting. Tools that act outside your company — sending, publishing, paying — are supervised and marked high risk.
approvals.s2p: Each approval shows who proposed it, a one-line summary of the effect and the details. Approve to let it run, or reject it with a reason.
approvals.s3p: An AI employee never says something was sent or done unless the tool actually succeeded. If a provider isn't connected, the task says so.

brain.title: Company Brain
brain.summary: Give your AI team your documents and get answers with sources.
brain.s1p: Upload documents to the Company Brain. They are processed so every AI role can search them, always within your own company.
brain.s2p: Ask a question in the Brain and get an answer that cites the passages it used. When your documents don't cover a question, the answer says so.
brain.s3p: Company memory holds durable facts — decisions, conventions, numbers — that every AI task takes into account. AI employees also keep short notes from earlier tasks. The company graph connects customers, products, teams and people for context.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.summary: Connect the providers your company already uses.
integrations.s1p: Open Integrations and connect a provider. Credentials are encrypted at rest and only used for your company.
integrations.s2p: See every sync with its result and history, and manage incoming webhooks with their verification method and delivery log.
integrations.s3p: Features that need a provider show that it isn't connected, with a link to set it up. Nothing is recorded as sent without a working connection.

security.title: Roles and security
security.summary: Permissions, two-factor sign-in, single sign-on and the audit log.
security.s1p: Every request — from a person or an AI tool — is checked against permissions scoped to the organization or a company. Data from one organization is never visible to another.
security.s2p: Turn on two-factor authentication for your account, and use single sign-on where your organization has set it up.
security.s3p: Changes, approvals and sensitive actions are written to the audit log together with the change itself, so the record is always complete.

languages.title: Languages and regions
languages.summary: Use Realy in five languages and see prices for your market.
languages.s1p: Realy is available in English, German, Arabic, Hindi and Chinese. Switch at any time from the language menu; your choice is remembered on your profile.
languages.s2p: In Arabic the whole interface switches to a right-to-left layout, including navigation and direction-dependent icons.
languages.s3p: Dates, numbers and money follow your locale. Plans are priced per country and shown in that country's currency.

whatIs.a: Realy is an AI business operating system. It brings your departments — sales, marketing, finance, people, projects, product, support and operations — into one platform and gives them an AI workforce that works under your approval.

aiActs.q: Can the AI change things without asking me?
aiActs.a: No. AI employees read on their own, but every change to your data is filed as an approval request, and anything external such as sending an email is marked high risk and waits for a person.

aiCost.a: Every task is tracked with its usage. Daily usage limits and per-task limits keep spending predictable, and you can pause any AI employee at any time.

data.q: Who can see my company's data?
data.a: Only people and AI roles in your organization with the right permissions. Every request is checked against permissions and data never crosses between organizations.

connect.q: Can I connect the tools I already use?
connect.a: Yes. Connect providers in Integrations; credentials are stored encrypted. When a provider isn't connected, Realy tells you instead of pretending something happened.

team.a: Yes. Invite people by email and give them roles for the whole organization or a single company.

security.a: Yes. You can protect your account with two-factor authentication, and organizations can use single sign-on.

languages.a: English, German, Arabic (right-to-left), Hindi and Chinese — across the whole product.

pricing.a: Plans are priced per country and shown in your local currency on the pricing page, with taxes calculated at checkout.

waitlist.a: Realy is opening market by market. If sign-up isn't open where you are yet, join the waitlist and we'll let you know as soon as it is.
